newsitem.title: CANADA: Yet another Zaire meeting needed - Canada minister.
newsitem.headline: Yet another Zaire meeting needed - Canada minister.

text.p: Another international political meeting will be required after Friday's military talks in Stuttgart, Germany, to decide whether to send a military force into Zaire, Canadian Defence Minister Doug Young said.
"There is no other way to determine it except by a meeting of the countries who would be involved," he told reporters who asked whether a new political gathering would be needed.

International aid agencies are increasingly expressing frustration with the long series of meetings and delays in mounting a Canadian-led mission to help refugees and displaced people in eastern Zaire. But the situation is so fluid and the number and locations of refugees so unclear that planners have not yet been able to make clear recommendations.
Complicating the situation has been the reluctance of the government in neighbouring Rwanda to allow a military operation to be mounted from its soil.

Young said Friday's meeting of military planners in Stuttgart, spilling over into the weekend, would lay out options for a possible military mission. "It's obvious that there is still a need for humanitarian aid. The question will be whether or not military intervention is required to be able to provide that," he said.
He said political assessment could begin this weekend or early next week on the basis of the Stuttgart talks but gave no details about possible dates or venues for a new meeting.

"The recommendations, which will really as far as I'm concerned only provide an array of options in terms of the military situation, would then be submitted to the various participating countries for political assessment," he said. "That will be done after the meeting in Stuttgart, I expect over the weekend and perhaps into the beginning of next week."

The U.N. Security Council approved a military mission a week ago but the sudden return of half a million refugees to Rwanda necessitated a re-evaluation of plans. Diplomats met in New York on Wednesday, military officers started in Stuttgart on Friday -- two days later than originally planned -- and aid officials were scheduled to meet in Geneva on Saturday.

Young said the figure of 700,000 remaining refugees advanced by office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees "seems to us a little high," but he added that it was difficult to arrive at a clear total.
On Thursday, Canadian Lt. Gen. Maurice Baril had a look for himself, flying over eastern Zaire near the Rwandan border at a relatively low altitude, Young added.
